# Part III — Implementation Plan (struct-canonical redesign + dual-track migration)

> Build spec for the team. Builds directly on Part I (render-surface architecture; "Architecture B" as the canonical store) and Part II (journal-template registry; **swap-not-rewrite**). Where Part I sequenced D→B as a *hedge*, the owner has since **locked Architecture B for all NEW projects** and a **dual-track strangler** for the live corpus. This plan executes that locked decision. Terminology (struct = front-matter-as-DATA + typed body blocks + `OpaqueBlock{rawLatex}` + bibliography + targetTemplate; the "themed approximation" surface; `compile_check`; the template registry's `template.yml`-style manifest; the conformance panel) is reused verbatim from Parts I & II.

---

## 1. Scope & locked decisions (recap)

These are settled. Do not relitigate.

- **No raw-LaTeX editor for new projects.** Users never see LaTeX. Interaction is **chat-primary**; a hidden file/directory system exists but is invisible; uploads/embeds happen by talking to the agent.
- **NEW projects' canonical source of truth = a STRUCTURED document model ("结构体" / struct)**, NOT a `.tex` file (Architecture B). The struct = `{front-matter as DATA}` + `{ordered body blocks}` + `{bibliography key→bib}` + `{targetTemplate}`. Full schema in §2.1.
- **The on-page editable surface = OUR themeable renderer of the struct → a "基本对齐 / roughly-aligned" APPROXIMATION** of the chosen journal format (NOT pixel-perfect), supporting free-typing + select→ask-AI. **Alongside it, a LIVE, EXACT PDF preview** compiled by `prism_tex` (per-template, pixel-exact). Exactness lives only in the PDF; the editable surface is explicitly "not 100%, roughly aligned is fine."
- **Journal templates = a REGISTRY.** Each template = official `.cls/.sty/.bst` (for compile) + a **style profile** (drives the renderer's themed approximation) + a **front-matter field mapping** (struct front-matter → that journal's macros). `set_journal_template` is a **DETERMINISTIC swap, never an LLM rewrite**. `prism_tex` must add `texlive-publishers`. Honest scope: "covered set + ~1hr porting per journal."
- **Export:** PDF via `prism_tex` (the authority, unchanged); Word `.docx` via **Pandoc FROM THE STRUCT** (not arbitrary LaTeX); LaTeX-file export = hand over the generated `.tex` (near-free).
- **Dual-track migration (strangler).** SAME menu/list; a **project-level NEW-vs-OLD distinction** keyed on a `schema_version` flag.
  - **NEW project (`schema_version='struct'`)** → entirely new logic (new struct surface + struct backend).
  - **OLD project (`schema_version='legacy'`)** → existing page/logic **UNCHANGED but READ-ONLY**: no edits (no agent edits, no manual edits), only **COMPILE + EXPORT (PDF / .tex; NOT docx — see §3)** allowed.
  - **NO lossy migration** of old LaTeX into the struct. Escape hatch = **clone-old-into-new** (fresh start, body carried as one `OpaqueBlock{rawLatex}`).

This is **live in production**. Every step below is additive, idempotent, and individually rollback-safe.

---

## 2. Target architecture for NEW projects

### 2.1 The struct — field-level schema

The struct is the canonical content. It is the superset front-matter schema from Part II §3 + typed body blocks from the locked decision. **Recommendation: store it as ONE JSON document column (`doc_struct LONGTEXT`) on `prism_projects`, not as normalized child tables** — justification in §4.2.

```jsonc
// prism_projects.doc_struct  (versioned via prism_struct_versions; see §4.3)
{
  "structVersion": 1,                       // bump on schema-breaking changes; migration key
  "targetTemplate": "ieee-conf",            // registry key; mirrors prism_projects.target_template (=repurposed venue_template_key)
  "frontMatter": {
    "title": "…",
    "shortTitle": "…",                       // running head (IEEE/ACM)
    "authors": [
      {
        "id": "a1",                          // stable local id, referenced by affRefs
        "given": "Ada",                      // → \fnm{} (sn-jnl), name halves
        "family": "Lovelace",                // → \sur{}
        "email": "ada@x.edu",
        "orcid": "0000-0002-…",
        "corresponding": true,
        "affRefs": ["af1", "af2"],           // → \author[1,2] / \IEEEauthorblockA nesting / \inst{1}
        "extra": { "ieeeFunding": "…", "acmRole": "…" }  // journal-specific optionals
      }
    ],
    "affiliations": [
      { "id": "af1", "organization": "…", "department": "…",
        "addressline": "…", "city": "…", "state": "…", "postcode": "…", "country": "…" }
    ],
    "abstract": "…",                          // plain rich text; template decides \abstract{} vs env
    "keywords": ["…"],
    "extra": { "acmCCS": [...], "copyright": "…" }   // taxonomy fields with no cross-journal analog
  },
  "body": [                                   // ORDERED list of blocks
    { "id": "b1", "type": "heading", "level": 1, "text": "Introduction", "label": "sec:intro" },
    { "id": "b2", "type": "paragraph", "inlines": [
        { "t": "text", "v": "As shown in " },
        { "t": "cite", "key": "lovelace1843" },           // → \cite{key}; backed by bibliography
        { "t": "text", "v": ", performance " },
        { "t": "math", "latex": "O(n\\log n)" },          // inline math
        { "t": "text", "v": " holds." }
      ] },
    { "t": "displayMath", "id": "b3", "latex": "E = mc^2", "label": "eq:e" },
    { "type": "figure", "id": "b4", "asset": "fig1", "caption": "…", "label": "fig:1", "width": "0.8\\linewidth" },
    { "type": "table", "id": "b5", "rows": [[...]], "caption": "…", "label": "tab:1" },
    { "type": "list", "id": "b6", "ordered": false, "items": [ [<inlines>], ... ] },
    { "type": "opaque", "id": "b7", "rawLatex": "\\begin{algorithm}…\\end{algorithm}" }  // fallback, render-as-image
  ],
  "bibliography": {                           // key → BibTeX entry (single source of truth for both PDF & docx)
    "lovelace1843": "@article{lovelace1843, author={…}, title={…}, year={1843}}"
  },
  "assets": {                                 // logical id → hidden-file pointer (binary lives in MinIO)
    "fig1": { "fileId": 991, "relPath": "figures/fig1.png", "mime": "image/png" }
  }
}
```

**Invariants the renderer + serializer rely on:** every block has a stable `id`; `cite.key` must exist in `bibliography`; `figure.asset` must exist in `assets`; `opaque` blocks are sealed (agent-managed, rendered as a compiled image, never shown as code — Part I's van der Hoeven "conservative" pattern).

### 2.2 Canonical store

- **Truth:** `prism_projects.doc_struct` (current) + an append-only `prism_struct_versions` chain (mirrors the existing immutable-append discipline of `prism_file_versions`; §4.3).
- **Derived (never re-parsed):** the struct → `.tex` **projector** materializes the struct + selected template into the **same `prism_files`/`prism_file_versions` contract** that `gatherCurrent` already assembles. This is the load-bearing reuse decision: **one compile spine, not two** (verification gotcha "two compile spines — avoid"). The projector writes `main.tex` (+ `references.bib`, + materialized assets) into versions so `StartCompile`/`runCompile`/`gatherCurrent`/`OpenLatestPDF`/MinIO/react-pdf/the content-hash cache all work **verbatim**.

```
struct (canonical, JSON)  ──projector(template)──▶  prism_files/prism_file_versions (.tex/.bib)  ──gatherCurrent──▶  prism_tex  ──▶  PDF (MinIO)
        │                                                                                                                            │
        └──────────────── themeable renderer (style profile) ──▶ editable approximation surface          react-pdf ◀───────────────┘ (exact preview)
```

### 2.3 The themeable renderer (+ per-template style profile)

A **fixed program parameterized by per-template style profiles** (Part I: "a browser engine + CSS"). Input = struct; output = a roughly-aligned, editable rendition. The **style profile** (part of each registry entry) drives column count, title/author block layout, section font scale, abstract framing — enough to *evoke* the journal, never to match the PDF pixel-for-pixel. Truly-exotic layout is delegated to the **exact PDF preview** (and to `OpaqueBlock`).

- Math: KaTeX for display; inline math via KaTeX, editable via a MathLive `<math-field>` NodeView (Part I §5.3). `cite` inlines render as "(Lovelace, 1843)".
- `opaque` blocks render as the `prism_tex`-compiled image of that fragment (read-only chip "agent-managed region").

### 2.4 The two surfaces

1. **Editable approximation** (themeable renderer, §2.3) — primary center pane. Free-typing for trivial edits (typo, bold, reword) applied directly to the struct; structural/scientific edits routed to the agent via **select→ask-AI** (Part I G1/G2/G4).
2. **Exact live PDF preview** — react-pdf over the `prism_tex` PDF, recompiled on change (debounced), last-good-PDF stays visible during recompile (Part I §6.6). This is the authority the user trusts for "what my advisor/the journal sees."

### 2.5 Chat-primary interaction

The single agent chat box is the command surface for everything structural and all uploads/embeds. Reuses `usePrismChat` + `PrismChatPanel` + the WS/round plumbing + autoname, all doc-model-agnostic at transport. Agent edits land as **rendered tracked changes** on surface (1) with margin `change_summary` chips (Part I §6.4).

### 2.6 Journal-template registry

`go:embed` under `backend/internal/prism/templates/<key>/` (mirrors `internal/content`). Each entry:
- `manifest.yml` — human metadata (name, single/two-column, page limit, doc-types, bib style), `parts` (`required`/`max_words`), `options` (typed knobs), and the **front-matter field map** (how struct front-matter projects onto this journal's macros).
- official `.cls`/`.sty`/`.bst` (or rely on `texlive-publishers`; bundle only for version pinning).
- `skeleton.tex.tmpl` — the projector template (jtex-style slots `[-CONTENT-]`, `[-IMPORTS-]`, `[- frontMatter.title -]`).
- `style-profile.json` — drives the renderer (§2.3).

Start with **3 spanning the three binding models**: `ieee-conf` (IEEEtran, nested), `elsarticle` (label), `sn-jnl` (index, `\abstract{}`-as-command). The field map is a **per-template deterministic renderer**, never LLM output.

### 2.7 Export

- **PDF** — `prism_tex`, unchanged (the projector feeds it clean LaTeX).
- **Word `.docx`** — **Pandoc from the struct** (struct → clean Markdown/Pandoc-AST → `--citeproc` + `reference.docx` → docx). Runs in the **agent/export container, NOT `prism_tex`** (the two-sandbox invariant; Part I §7.2). `--bibliography` from the same `bibliography` map; figures pre-rasterized (`poppler-utils`).
- **LaTeX `.tex`** — hand over the projector's generated `.tex` (near-free).

### 2.8 New ↔ concrete pieces map

| Concern | Reuse as-is | Build new |
|---|---|---|
| Compile / PDF / cache / MinIO | `StartCompile`, `runCompile`, `gatherCurrent`, `OpenLatestPDF`, `prism_tex`, `texclient`, react-pdf, content-hash cache | — |
| Chat / WS / round / autoname | `usePrismChat`, `PrismChatPanel`, WS pipe, `IssueWSTicket`, `agent_sessions` binding, `OnTitleResult`→`handleAgentTitle` | agent struct-op protocol (§7) |
| Versioning discipline | immutable-append pattern (copy from `prism_file_versions`) | `prism_struct_versions` table |
| Front-matter / body editing | — | struct renderer + editable surface + struct CRUD endpoints |
| Templates | dormant `venue_template_key` column (repurpose) | registry (`go:embed`), projector, style profiles |
| Export | `OpenLatestPDF` (PDF), `.tex` handoff | Pandoc docx-from-struct |

---

## 3. Dual-track migration strategy (core of this plan)

This is the safety-critical part. The system is **LIVE**; the legacy path stays untouched and is merely *frozen*.

### 3.1 The flag

**ONE additive column on the single project-level row, `prism_projects`:**

```
schema_version VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'legacy'
```

- Lives on `prism_projects` (the confirmed one-row-per-project entity; `0009_prism_fields.sql:19`). Added via `add_column_if_not_exists` → **every existing live row backfills to `'legacy'` with zero data movement** (mirrors the dormant `venue_template_key` precedent at `0009_prism_fields.sql:24`).
- **Do NOT add a second flag.** `schema_version` is the single source of the split.
- `target_template` = **reuse the existing dormant `venue_template_key`** (`model.go:64`, confirmed zero reads/writes anywhere) — do not add a parallel column.
- New projects are minted `schema_version='struct'` by `CreateProject` — **flip this as the FINAL ship step** (§3.10), so until then `schema_version` is dormant metadata exactly like `venue_template_key` was (zero behavior change, zero risk).

It must be added to the serialized `Project` JSON returned by **both** `ListProjects` and `GetProject` (`model.go:59-71` → add `SchemaVersion string`), so the frontend can route per-row at both the list and open-project layers with no extra request (grounding confirms it rides `useProjects()` and `useProject()` for free).

### 3.2 What makes an OLD project read-only — the gated endpoints

Read-only is enforced **server-side at the service/handler layer, not UI-hidden** (UI hiding is necessary but insufficient — a stray write path silently mutates a "frozen" project). The minimal chokepoint already exists: every HTTP handler funnels through `Handler.ownedProject` (`handler.go:32`), which already loads + ownership-checks and **returns the `*Project`**.

**Mechanism:**
```go
func (p *Project) ReadOnly() bool { return p.SchemaVersion == "legacy" }
var ErrReadOnlyProject = ... // typed, friendly: "该项目为旧版项目,仅支持查看 / 编译 / 导出"
```
In `ownedProject`, after the ownership check, group-A handlers gain one guard line: `if p.ReadOnly() { utils.SafeBadRequest(c, ErrReadOnlyProject); return }`. For WS/round methods that re-fetch via `GetProject`, put the same guard inside the service method after the fetch.

**MUST be blocked for `schema_version='legacy'` (group A — the write surface):**

| Endpoint | Handler / location | Why blocked |
|---|---|---|
| `PUT /projects/:id/files/:fileId` | `SaveFile` (`handler.go:228` → `service.go:156`) | appends a version |
| `POST /projects/:id/files` | `CreateFile` (`handler.go:170`, `files.go`) | new file |
| `POST /projects/:id/files/:fileId/rename` | `RenameFile` (`handler.go:189`) | mutates manifest |
| `DELETE /projects/:id/files/:fileId` | `DeleteFile` (`handler.go:212`) | deletes |
| `POST /projects/:id/files/:fileId/versions/:versionId/restore` | `RestoreVersion` (`handler.go:360`, `history.go`) | writes new current |
| `POST /projects/:id/cite/apply` | `CiteApply` (`handler.go:400` → `cite.go:48`) | appends `references.bib` |
| `PATCH /projects/:id` | `UpdateProject` (`handler.go:86` → `service.go:103`) | renames |
| `POST /projects/:id/round/apply` | `ApplyRound` (`handler_ws.go:92` → `ws_round.go:121`) | **the only path that commits agent edits to DB — the one that MUST be blocked for integrity** |
| `POST /projects/:id/ws-ticket` | `IssueWSTicket` (`handler_ws.go:33`) | **freezes chat entirely** (decision below) |
| `POST /projects/:id/round/prepare` | `PrepareRound` (`handler_ws.go:57`) | no DB write but only meaningful for editing — defense-in-depth |
| `POST /projects/:id/round/reject` | `RejectRound` (`handler_ws.go:119`) | same |
| auto-title write | `handleAgentTitle` (`autoname.go:33`) | add `if proj.ReadOnly() { return }` early — only matters if chat were on; with chat frozen it never fires |

> `DeleteProject` (`handler.go:106`) is a **policy call** — deleting an OLD project loses no editability. Decision: **keep DeleteProject enabled** for legacy (users must be able to clean up their list). Document this explicitly.

### 3.3 What stays enabled (compile + export, read paths)

Compile/export is **already fully decoupled from editing** — `runCompile`→`gatherCurrent` reads only `prism_file_versions.body` (DB current) and writes only to `prism_compiles` + MinIO; it shares **no mutating code** with the write paths. So read-only **cannot break compile/export**. Keep enabled (group B, untouched):

`GetProject`, `ListProjects`, `GetFile`, `ListVersions`, `Compile` (`handler.go:255`→`service.go:246`), `GetCompile`, `GetPDF`, `CiteSearch` (the read sibling of `CiteApply` — **gate by handler, not URL prefix**, they share `/cite`), `GetWSMessages` (chat history replay — read), `GetContext`, `PendingRound`, `ReadWorkspaceFile`.

### 3.4 Agent chat behavior on old projects — FROZEN

**Decision: fully freeze chat on legacy projects.** `IssueWSTicket` returns `ErrReadOnlyProject`; no WS, no round/apply. Rationale (verification): a chat that can talk but can never apply an edit is worse UX than no chat; it also leaks (a) the auto-title write and (b) AI quota + a held agent session for a project the user can't edit. Freezing removes the entire surface (and the title-write edge case) with one gate.

- **Do NOT eagerly delete existing legacy `agent_session_id` rows** on deploy (data-loss-ish + reconcile churn). Just stop issuing tickets; idle agent sessions expire on the agent side.
- **Billing is untouched** because legacy never enters the WS/quota path. (If we ever allowed read-only Q&A chat — we don't — it would still consume tokens and MUST keep firing `PreUserMessage`/`OnMessageComplete`. We avoid that trap by freezing.)

### 3.5 Shared-infra handling

- **`agent_sessions` table & reconcile loop:** legacy and struct projects coexist in the same table (each keyed by `owner_id`; `uk_owner` from `0014_agent_sessions_owner.sql`); no schema conflict. The `mode`/`schema_version` flag gates whether a session may be *created/used*, not the table. The bootstrap reconcile loop may keep mapping legacy `agent_session_id`→`agent_sessions` rows harmlessly — **do NOT start deleting legacy sessions** (that would make the loop re-create orphan bindings). Self-heal invariant for struct projects is preserved as long as we only ever *stop issuing tickets* for legacy, never delete.
- **`prism_tex`:** shared, unchanged for legacy; gets `texlive-publishers` added for struct templates (additive, safe for legacy — more classes available, none removed).
- **Quota:** struct projects use the same `spec.go` `PreUserMessage` (vip daily quota) + `OnMessageComplete` (`llm_token_usage`) hooks, per-message, unchanged. Legacy bypasses them by being frozen.
- **Autoname / `OnTitleResult`:** struct track reuses the same sink writing `prism_projects.title`; legacy never fires it. The shared list shows consistent names for both tracks (same column).

### 3.6 Clone-old-into-new (non-lossy fresh start) escape hatch

A new endpoint `POST /projects/:id/clone-to-struct` ("从此项目新建一个新版项目"):
- Creates a **fresh `schema_version='struct'`** project seeded from the chosen journal-template **default struct**.
- Carries the **entire legacy body as a SINGLE `OpaqueBlock{rawLatex}`** (the struct model's own fallback node), plus any trivially-modeled `title`. **Never auto-parses arbitrary LaTeX into typed blocks** — that is exactly the lossy import the owner rejected (Part I v8: 2%–54% converter success).
- The user, via the agent, then progressively restructures the opaque block into typed blocks.
- Framed as "**create a new-version project from this**," not "upgrade." The original legacy project is untouched (still compile/export-able).

### 3.7 Shared menu/list UX with new/old labeling

Same sidebar list (`PrismProjectSidebar`), default sort by `updated_at` (existing `idx_user` — legacy projects naturally sink over time). Each row carries `schema_version`; render a per-row badge for legacy: **"旧版 · 只读"**. Click routes to the correct surface based on `schema_version` (§6.1). The list is the only place both tracks visibly coexist.

### 3.8 WHY no lossy auto-import

The struct (front-matter-as-DATA + typed blocks + `OpaqueBlock` fallback) **genuinely cannot be reconstructed from arbitrary LaTeX** without the constrained-parser-with-opaque-fallback risk the owner refuses to ship on live data (Part I §8 Phase 3 caveat; v8's 2%–54% number; TeXpert 0–17.5% on hard tasks). Legacy bodies are immutable-append `longtext` with no size/row constraint forcing migration — **freezing is a flag check, not a data move.** Auto-import would risk silently corrupting users' real, in-production papers. The clone-to-struct opaque-block path gives "start fresh, keep my text reachable" without that risk.

### 3.9 Rollback / feature-flag safety (LIVE system)

- The migration is **additive + non-destructive** (`add_column_if_not_exists`, default `'legacy'`). Rollback of the schema is never needed.
- The **struct track ships behind an env/feature flag** (`PRISM_STRUCT_ENABLED`); the read-only guards are **inert until `CreateProject` flips to mint `'struct'`** (because while everything is legacy and editable, you simply don't flip creation yet).
- **Rollback at any point = flip `CreateProject` back to minting `'legacy'` / feature-flag off the struct surface.** No data migration to undo.
- **The only irreversible-ish actions to NEVER do:** (a) delete legacy `agent_session_id` rows; (b) rewrite legacy `prism_file_versions.body`. Either is the sole way this strangler could cause data loss. Forbidden.

### 3.10 Ship order (each step independently safe)

1. **Additive migration** — all rows `'legacy'`, dormant. Zero behavior change.
2. **Struct track behind feature flag** — new tables + projector + endpoints + frontend, not reachable in prod.
3. **Server-side read-only guards** keyed on `schema_version` — land them *together with* step 4 (they're inert before).
4. **Flip `CreateProject` to mint `'struct'` + activate guards** — only when the struct surface is production-ready. This is the cutover.

## 4. Data model changes

All additive, idempotent, following the repo's `NNNN_*_fields/_indexes/_defaults` convention + `0000_utils` procedures. **Latest existing prism migration is `0010_prism_edits.sql` (no `0011`); `0012_prism_chat.sql` is the last prism-named file. Pick the next free global numbers** — verify with `ls docker/mysql/migrations/` at implementation time (grounding shows live migrations up to `0070`; the FE grounding suggested `0044` but that's stale — **use the next free number after the highest existing file**, e.g. `00NN`).

### 4.1 The flag + template columns

```sql
-- 00NN_prism_struct_fields.sql
CALL add_column_if_not_exists('prism_projects','schema_version',"VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'legacy'");
-- target_template: REUSE the dormant venue_template_key. No new column. (model.go:64)
-- doc_struct: the canonical JSON store (see §4.2)
CALL add_column_if_not_exists('prism_projects','doc_struct','LONGTEXT NULL');
CALL add_column_if_not_exists('prism_projects','struct_version_id','BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL');  -- → prism_struct_versions.id (current)
```

No `_defaults` needed — the column default `'legacy'` backfills every live row. No `_indexes` needed for the flag (queries filter in-app on the already-loaded project; list order keeps using `idx_user`).

### 4.2 JSON column vs normalized child tables — RECOMMEND JSON column

**Recommendation: store the struct as one `doc_struct LONGTEXT` column + an append-only version chain. Do NOT normalize front-matter/blocks into child tables.**

Justification:
- The struct is **read/written as a whole** (the agent emits/maintains it; the renderer consumes it; the projector serializes it). There are no per-block queries that need SQL — block lookup is by `id` within the loaded JSON.
- It **mirrors the existing discipline exactly**: `prism_file_versions.body` is already a `longtext` immutable-append blob; `doc_struct` is the same pattern one level up. Reuse the proven `AppendCurrentVersion` transaction shape.
- Normalized tables (frontmatter/authors/affiliations/blocks rows) buy nothing (no cross-project block queries, no joins) and cost a large surface of new repository code + migration churn + multi-table transactional consistency.
- `LONGTEXT` (not MySQL `JSON` type) keeps it engine-agnostic and lets the projector/serializer own validation; charset `utf8mb4` (Part I memory: migration UTF-8 rule).

### 4.3 Struct version chain (immutable-append)

```sql
-- 00NN_prism_struct_fields.sql (cont.)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS prism_struct_versions (
  id              BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  project_id      BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  version_no      INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  doc_struct      LONGTEXT NOT NULL,            -- snapshot of the full struct
  struct_sha256   CHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  author          VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user',  -- user/agent/accepted (mirrors prism_file_versions)
  status          VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'current', -- pending/current/superseded
  base_version_id BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL,
  created_at      DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4;
```
```sql
-- 00NN_prism_struct_indexes.sql
CALL add_index_if_not_exists('prism_struct_versions','idx_proj_version','(project_id, version_no)', FALSE);
CALL add_index_if_not_exists('prism_struct_versions','idx_proj_status','(project_id, status)', FALSE);
```

Save = insert new version, supersede old `current`, re-point `prism_projects.struct_version_id` — same transaction shape as `AppendCurrentVersion` (`repository.go:245`). `prism_projects.doc_struct` holds a denormalized copy of the current snapshot for cheap reads.

### 4.4 Template registry — `go:embed`, NOT a table

Templates are code-shaped artifacts (`.cls`, Jinja-ish `.tex`, manifest, style profile) versioned with the binary. **`go:embed backend/internal/prism/templates/<key>/`** (mirrors `internal/content`). No DB table; the dormant `venue_template_key`/`target_template` column on `prism_projects` is the only per-project anchor.

### 4.5 Migration file list to add

- `00NN_prism_struct_fields.sql` — `schema_version`, `doc_struct`, `struct_version_id` columns + `prism_struct_versions` table.
- `00NN+1_prism_struct_indexes.sql` — the two indexes above.
- (No `_defaults` — column default + `go:embed` registry cover it.)

**Never** `DROP`. The `prism_chat_messages` stranded table stays; do not touch it.

## 5. Backend changes

New code lives in `backend/internal/prism/` alongside the existing module (one module, two tracks).

### 5.1 New struct module pieces

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `struct_model.go` | Go structs for the §2.1 schema; JSON (de)serialize + validation (ids unique, cite keys resolve, asset refs resolve). |
| `struct_repository.go` | `GetStruct`, `AppendStructVersion` (immutable-append, mirrors `repository.go:245`), `ListStructVersions`, `RestoreStructVersion`. |
| `struct_service.go` | struct CRUD business logic; struct→.tex projection orchestration; struct→docx export. |
| `struct_handler.go` | HTTP layer; reuses `ownedProject`. |
| `projector.go` | **struct + template → `.tex` + `.bib` + materialized assets**, written into `prism_files`/`prism_file_versions` so `gatherCurrent` is reused verbatim. Deterministic; per-template field map from the registry. |
| `templates/registry.go` | `go:embed` loader; `Get(key) → manifest + skeleton + style profile + .cls list`; exposes style profiles to the frontend. |
| `docx.go` | struct → Pandoc (export container) → `.docx`; uses `bibliography` map + `--citeproc` + `reference.docx`; pre-rasterizes figures. |

### 5.2 New endpoints (under `/api/v1/user/prism`, registered in `routes_user.go`)

| Method + path | Handler | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /projects/:id/struct` | `GetStruct` | returns current `doc_struct` (struct projects only) |
| `PUT /projects/:id/struct` | `SaveStruct` | direct user edit (typo/bold/reword); append struct version; triggers projector + compile |
| `PATCH /projects/:id/struct/frontmatter` | `SaveFrontMatter` | form-driven front-matter edits |
| `POST /projects/:id/struct/ops` | `ApplyStructOps` | **agent-emitted struct ops** committed via the round path (replaces file-diff `ApplyRound` for struct track) |
| `GET /projects/:id/struct/versions` + `.../restore` | struct history | mirrors legacy version history |
| `POST /projects/:id/template` | `SetJournalTemplate` | **deterministic swap**; sets `target_template`, re-runs projector, returns conformance report |
| `GET /templates` | `ListTemplates` | registry metadata + style profiles for the picker |
| `POST /projects/:id/export/docx` | `ExportDocx` | struct→Pandoc→docx (struct track only) |
| `GET /projects/:id/export/tex` | `ExportTex` | hand over projector `.tex` (both tracks: legacy = current body bytes, struct = projected) |
| `POST /projects/:id/clone-to-struct` | `CloneToStruct` | escape hatch (§3.6) |

Compile/PDF endpoints are **shared, unchanged** — struct projects compile through the same `Compile`/`GetCompile`/`GetPDF` after the projector has written `.tex` into versions.

### 5.3 Read-only gating mechanism

As specified in §3.2: `Project.ReadOnly()` + one guard line in `ownedProject` for group-A HTTP handlers, + the guard inside `ApplyRound`/`IssueWSTicket`/`PrepareRound`/`RejectRound` service methods after their `GetProject`, + early return in `handleAgentTitle`. Typed `ErrReadOnlyProject`.

### 5.4 Reuse of texclient / prism_tex; texlive-publishers

- **`texclient` / `prism_tex` unchanged in behavior** for both tracks — the projector funnels struct projects into the identical `gatherCurrent` contract.
- **Add `texlive-publishers` (+ likely `texlive-fonts-extra` for acmart) to `prism_tex/Dockerfile`** — the single hard blocker for journal classes (Part II §6). Additive; legacy compiles unaffected.
- Extend `gatherCurrent` (or the projector) to **materialize `KindAsset` from MinIO** when a template/figure needs a binary (today assets are skipped — `service.go:200`). Needed for struct figures.

### 5.5 Agent edit protocol change

The agent stops hand-writing `.tex` for struct projects and instead emits **struct ops** (§7). Backend `ApplyStructOps` validates ops against the loaded struct (exactly-once anchor match — guard the Part I #9434 silent-no-op bug), applies them, appends a struct version, runs the projector, recompiles. `set_journal_template` is handled **deterministically server-side**, not by the LLM.

## 7. Agent changes

The agent stops authoring journal LaTeX and instead **maintains the struct + picks the template**. Tools/skills (via the existing `--add-dir /prism-add` channel and the agent's tool registry):

1. **`emit_struct_ops(ops[])`** — the agent's primary edit verb. Ops are anchored by block `id` (insert-after/replace/delete block; edit inlines; set front-matter field; add bibliography entry). Each op carries a plain-language `change_summary`. Backend validates exactly-once anchor match before claiming success (Part I #9434 guard). **The agent never emits `.tex` for struct projects.**
2. **`set_journal_template(key, options)`** — **declares intent only**; the **deterministic server-side projector** performs the swap (struct front-matter → that journal's macros via the registry field map). The agent's only post-swap action is **content adaptation** (shorten to page limit, move to appendix) — **never macro surgery** (Part II §6: TeXpert 0–17.5% trap; DeepSeek package-hallucination).
3. **`set_frontmatter(fields)`** — validates against the journal schema (e.g. elsarticle needs `organization`/`country`; corresponding author needs email). Missing fields → **ask the user**, never invent macros.
4. **`compile_check`** — compile in `prism_tex`; **parse the `.log`** (localized, not raw dump — Part II §5): (a) errors → nearest block, (b) Overfull \hbox / column overflow, (c) page count vs registry page-limit. Surface as plain-language fix tasks. Bounded retries (~3) extracting the specific failure, last-good fallback (Part I §6.6).
5. **upload-via-chat placement** — attached file lands read-only in session cwd → agent inserts a `figure`/table/`cite` block + registers the asset in `struct.assets`; user sees only the rendered figure.

**Keeping the agent from hand-writing journal macros:** the system prompt + per-journal format skill expose the **struct schema and the registry manifest as the conformance spec** (jtex `template.yml` model); `set_journal_template` is the *only* path to journal LaTeX, and it is deterministic. The agent declares `packages` via the template, never `\usepackage` ad hoc. `OpaqueBlock` is the sanctioned escape for genuinely un-modelable fragments (rendered as an image, never shown as code).

> Agent + backend **must deploy together** (project rule, prior memory): the struct-op protocol and `ApplyStructOps` are a matched pair.

---

## 8. Phased roadmap with milestones

Read-only freeze is **EARLY** (live-system safety); the smallest end-to-end struct prototype is **first** within the build track.

### Phase 0 — Flag + read-only freeze (safety first)
- **Deliverables:** `00NN_prism_struct_fields.sql` (schema_version default `'legacy'`, + struct columns/table — struct columns dormant); `SchemaVersion` on `Project` + JSON in `ListProjects`/`GetProject`; `Project.ReadOnly()` + guards on all group-A endpoints (§3.2); `LegacyPrismWorkspace` fork = read-only UI; `PrismPage.tsx:47` branch (struct branch points at a stub behind the feature flag). `IssueWSTicket` frozen for legacy.
- **Milestone (demoable):** an existing production project opens in the legacy workspace, **compiles + exports PDF + downloads .tex**, but every edit/chat path is server-rejected with the friendly error. New projects still mint `'legacy'` (no behavior change yet).
- **De-risk:** proves the freeze is airtight on real live data *before* any struct code is reachable. Rollback = trivial (flag dormant).

### Phase 1 — Struct spine + projector (one compile spine)
- **Deliverables:** `struct_model.go`/`struct_repository.go`/`struct_service.go`; `prism_struct_versions` save path; `projector.go` (struct→.tex/.bib into `prism_file_versions`); **one** journal template in the registry (`ieee-conf`) with manifest + skeleton + style profile; `texlive-publishers` in `prism_tex/Dockerfile`; `GET/PUT /projects/:id/struct`.
- **Milestone:** a struct (authored by hand/seed) **projects to `.tex`, compiles via the existing `Compile` path, renders an exact PDF** in react-pdf. No agent yet.
- **De-risk:** proves struct→.tex→compile reuses the existing spine verbatim (no second compile path). This is **the smallest end-to-end new-track prototype** (§9).

### Phase 2 — Renderer + editable surface + struct chat
- **Deliverables:** `StructRenderer` (style-profile-driven approximation); front-matter form; direct free-typing → `SaveStruct`; `PrismWorkspaceV2` wiring exact PDF preview + chat (reused) + sources chips; agent `emit_struct_ops` + `ApplyStructOps` (round path); select→ask-AI + rendered tracked changes.
- **Milestone:** a user opens a struct project, free-types a paragraph, selects text and asks the agent to rephrase, **sees the change as a rendered tracked-change + the exact PDF update — never a `\command`.**
- **De-risk:** validates "agent reliably emits valid struct ops" and "renderer approximation is acceptable" — the two biggest UX unknowns (§9).

### Phase 3 — Journal templates (deterministic swap) + conformance
- **Deliverables:** registry grows to **3** (`ieee-conf`, `elsarticle`, `sn-jnl` — the three binding models); `set_journal_template` deterministic swap; `compile_check` with `.log` parsing (errors/overflow/page-limit); template picker + conformance panel.
- **Milestone:** the **same struct** retargets IEEE↔Elsevier↔Springer by picking a template; both compile; conformance panel flags page-limit/overflow. The Part II smallest-prototype thesis (same `authors[]` → `\IEEEauthorblockN` vs `\author[1]`+`\affiliation`) is proven in product.
- **De-risk:** proves swap-not-rewrite at product scale; "~1hr/journal porting" cost validated.

### Phase 4 — Export (docx) + clone-to-struct + cutover
- **Deliverables:** Pandoc `docx.go` (struct→docx in the export container; `--citeproc`, `reference.docx`, figure rasterization); `.tex` export both tracks; `clone-to-struct` escape hatch + list badge; **flip `CreateProject` to mint `'struct'`** + activate guards (the cutover).
- **Milestone:** new projects are born struct end-to-end (chat → struct → exact PDF → journal swap → PDF/docx/.tex export); a legacy project can be cloned into a fresh struct project carrying its body as one `OpaqueBlock`.
- **De-risk:** struct→docx fidelity measured on real papers; cutover is the last, reversible step.

### Phase 5 — Sunset hygiene (ongoing, low priority)
- Lazy-chunk the legacy editor bundle; nudge legacy users toward clone + export; keep legacy READ + compile backend **forever** (cheap, read-only). Never a destructive bulk migration.

**Week 1:** Phase 0 — the migration + read-only guards + legacy fork + branch. It's pure safety, ships behavioral-no-op (everything still legacy), and de-risks the live system before any struct code exists.

---

## 9. Risks, open questions, and the first prototype

**Riskiest unknowns:**
1. **Agent reliably emitting a VALID struct / struct ops.** The whole new track assumes the LLM produces schema-valid, anchor-resolvable ops. Mitigation: strict server-side validation + exactly-once anchor match + bounded retry with localized error feedback; `OpaqueBlock` as the always-available escape. *If the agent can't hit the struct reliably, the renderer approximation and the whole new track are at risk* — **prove this earliest (Phase 2).**
2. **Renderer / style-profile effort per template.** "基本对齐" lowers the bar (not pixel-perfect; exactness is in the PDF), but each journal still needs a style profile + a field map (~1hr/journal claim from Part II is the bet). Risk = the approximation feels wrong enough that users distrust it. Mitigation: the exact PDF preview is always one pane over; the approximation only needs to be *navigable + editable*, not faithful.
3. **Struct→docx fidelity** (Pandoc from struct). Best-effort; OMML math survives only from clean source (which the struct guarantees), but tables/cross-refs/citations need `--citeproc` + `pandoc-crossref` (version-locked) + figure rasterization. Mitigation: ship with a "best-effort, touch up in Word" disclaimer; docx is **struct-track-only** (legacy has no struct → legacy export = PDF + .tex only; do NOT promise docx on legacy).
4. **Read-only freeze airtightness on the LIVE corpus.** A single un-guarded write path silently mutates a "frozen" production paper. Mitigation: server-side guard at the `ownedProject` chokepoint covering the enumerated group-A set; Phase 0 ships and verifies this before any struct surface exists.

**Open questions:**
- Does the editable approximation surface need direct-typed math editing (MathLive everywhere) in v1, or is "select math → ask agent" enough? Lean: MathLive NodeView for inline/display math from Phase 2.
- Keep a hidden "view generated .tex (advanced)" toggle for power users (Part I open question)? Lean: yes, off by default, read-only.

**The single smallest prototype that proves the new track end-to-end (Phase 1 milestone):**
> Hand-author one struct JSON (front-matter + a few body blocks + one cite) → run `projector.go` with the `ieee-conf` template → it writes `main.tex` + `references.bib` into `prism_file_versions` → the **existing** `Compile` path produces a PDF in MinIO → react-pdf renders the exact preview. **No agent, no new compile path, no LaTeX shown.** If this loop works, the struct-canonical track reuses the entire compile/PDF spine verbatim and the rest is renderer + agent + registry population. Immediately after, the Part II swap-prototype: render the *same* struct through `elsarticle` and diff the title pages — if the same `authors[]` yields the right macros in both, swap-not-rewrite is proven.

<!-- Part V appended by a 7-agent rendered-diff research workflow. -->

# Part V — Rendered (Word-like) tracked-changes diff, replacing the code-diff

## 1. Recommendation (decisive)

- **Diff at the STRUCT level, not the markdown text or rendered HTML.** We already hold OLD struct (`useStruct(projectId)` → `structQ.data`, `PrismWorkspaceV2.tsx:35`) and can cheaply obtain NEW struct (backend already runs `parseEditorMarkdown(wf.Content)` at apply time in `struct_service.go:216`). Diff the two structs with a **two-phase algorithm**: (a) LCS block alignment with a similarity threshold, then (b) word-level inline diff only inside blocks judged "modified." This is the only altitude that preserves KaTeX/figure fidelity **and** keeps every change addressable back to the canonical struct.
- **Render inline via a dedicated `StructDiffRenderer`, NOT by re-serializing "diff markdown."** Reuse the existing `StructRenderer`/`MarkdownRenderer` block renderers for unchanged and inserted content; wrap only the *delta* runs in styled `<ins>`/`<del>` React components. Injecting diff markers back into a markdown string and re-parsing is fragile around block and `$…$` boundaries — that is a milder version of the exact problem that sinks the text-diff approach.
- **Treat math / figure / displayMath / opaque blocks and inline `math` runs as ATOMIC.** Any change → delete-old + insert-new (old KaTeX struck/dimmed, new KaTeX highlighted, side by side). Never char-diff TeX. This is the single most important correctness rule on a KaTeX surface.
- **Deletions stay in place, struck-through** (Google Docs / OOXML `w:delText` model), not collapsed — the reader sees what left.
- **Accept/reject: ship WHOLE-TURN in v1, per-change in v2.** Whole-turn (`chat.apply()` = adopt NEW, `chat.reject()` = keep OLD) is already wired and is the mainstream AI-editor baseline (Notion AI, ChatGPT Canvas whole-rewrites do exactly this — see verification v2). The **same diff data structure upgrades to per-change with no rework**: per-block, then per-inline-hunk (Docs/Word gold standard).
- **Add a "Reviewing" vs "Clean" view toggle** on the right pane so the typeset reading experience is never permanently disrupted (Word Simple-vs-All-Markup / ChatGPT clean-vs-Show-changes).
- **Deprecate `LatexDiffEditor` in the struct track.** In `PrismWorkspaceV2.tsx:262`, replace `<LatexDiffEditor original={…} proposed={…} displayOnly />` with `<StructDiffRenderer old={…} new={…} onAccept/onReject/>`. `LatexDiffEditor` (CodeMirror 6 `unifiedMergeView` + `StreamLanguage(stex)`) is the raw-markdown code pane the owner wants gone; it may remain only for any legacy file-diff path (`ws_round.go` non-struct branch), not the struct workspace.
- **New dependency: add `diff` (jsdiff).** No diff lib is currently installed (verified: `package.json` has no `diff`/`diff-match-patch`/`jsondiffpatch`). jsdiff gives us both `diffArrays` (block alignment with a custom comparator) and `diffWordsWithSpace` (intra-block, with `Intl.Segmenter` for CJK) in one small dep.

## 2. The core decision — where to diff

**Chosen: struct-level, two-phase (align blocks → word-diff inline runs).** Reject the two alternatives:

- **Markdown-text diff (jsdiff `diffWords` on `structToEditorMarkdown(old)` vs `new_body`)** — this is essentially today's data path (both bodies are the same restricted dialect). Cheap, but markdown punctuation (`#`, `**`, `_`, `$…$`, `- `, `[@key]`) pollutes word tokens: a heading-level change or a re-delimited math run renders as garbage ins/del, and an accepted hunk maps to a *markdown range*, not a struct block — write-back is guesswork. Viable only as a fallback inside a single `opaque` block.
- **Rendered-HTML diff (htmldiff.js)** — tempting because it emits real `<ins>/<del>/.diffmod` and is tag-aware. But it diffs *post-render* HTML we don't control (react-markdown + KaTeX output changes across versions → non-deterministic), and **KaTeX is the killer**: KaTeX emits deep `<span class="katex">…</span>` MathML+HTML trees, and htmldiff's own docs warn that inserting `<ins>/<del>` inside `\(…\)`/math wrappers **corrupts rendering** — you'd have to register KaTeX wrappers as atomic, at which point you're doing opaque replacement anyway, but on brittle HTML instead of on the clean struct. Accept/reject would map to HTML ranges, not struct nodes. Good only for a throwaway read-only redline.

**Why struct wins (the math/KaTeX fidelity argument, verification v1 — held):** matched math/figure blocks render *unchanged* through the existing `StructRenderer` → `MarkdownRenderer` → `rehype-katex` pass — **zero KaTeX-diff noise** — because we never let a differ split inside `$…$` or a `<span class="katex">` tree. Only genuinely-changed text runs get `<ins>/<del>` wrapping. And every marked change carries a struct address (blockIndex + run path + offset), which is exactly what per-change accept/reject needs.

**Two-phase algorithm (from markdown-diff-viewer / TipTap `smart` mode / Liveblocks copilot, all verified):**
1. **Block alignment.** `jsdiff.diffArrays(oldBlocks, newBlocks, { comparator })`. Comparator matches by **stable id if present, else `type` + normalized-content hash**. ⚠️ Grounding warning: `parseEditorMarkdown` **reassigns fresh ids** (`b1,b2…`, `md_bridge.go:137,150`), so old↔new block ids are **not preserved** through the round-trip — align by **position + content similarity**, never by id. For an adjacent removed+added block pair of the same type, compute a similarity score (Dice coefficient on bigrams; markdown-diff-viewer's threshold ~40%): above → mark "modified" and recurse into phase 2; below → keep as delete-block + insert-block. A removed block whose content-hash reappears elsewhere in the added set → a **move** (badge it, don't double-count as delete+insert).
2. **Intra-block inline diff.** For a "modified" paragraph / heading / list-item, flatten inline runs to text (remembering run boundaries + marks), `jsdiff.diffWordsWithSpace(oldText, newText)` (add `{ intlSegmenter: new Intl.Segmenter('zh', {granularity:'word'}) }` for CJK), map tokens back onto runs, splitting runs at change boundaries and tagging each `unchanged | inserted | deleted`. Preserve marks so a bolded inserted word stays bold + green.

Only `title / abstract / keywords / body` change per round; authors / affiliations / bibliography / targetTemplate are invariant (`md_bridge.go:11-13`) — **don't diff them.**

## 3. Rendering the inline diff on react-markdown

**Build a dedicated `StructDiffRenderer` (recommend), do NOT emit diff-markdown for re-parsing.** The renderer walks the aligned diff tree (§2) and renders React directly, reusing the existing per-block renderers from `StructRenderer.tsx` (`bodyToMd`/`inlinesToMd` → `MarkdownRenderer`):

- **Unchanged block** → existing block renderer, full typeset fidelity (KaTeX/figure intact).
- **Modified paragraph/heading** → render runs normally, but changed spans emit `<ins className="diff-ins">` (green, underlined) and `<del className="diff-del">` (red strikethrough, **kept in place**). Since the inline schema is a tiny closed set (`text/bold/italic/cite/math`), render inline runs yourself and only invoke react-markdown + KaTeX for whole-math runs — this keeps ins/del wrapping outside the markdown parser.
- **Inserted block** → render new block normally inside a green left-gutter/banner + subtle tint.
- **Deleted block** → render old block dimmed/struck inside a red gutter, kept in place (don't collapse — mirrors `w:delText`).
- **Moved block** → "moved ↑/↓" badge at source (ghosted) and destination, not delete+insert.
- **Math / displayMath / inline `math` change** → a **before→after compare-chip**: struck old KaTeX → arrow → new KaTeX, both fully typeset. Never diff inside TeX.
- **Figure change** → added figure in green frame, deleted figure dimmed/struck in red frame, both with caption.
- **List** → align items via `diffArrays` (item-text hash) → per-item add/remove/changed; changed items get inline word-diff.
- **`opaque`** → block-level replace chip (old collapsed / new shown); last resort `diffLines` rendered as colored lines, never a code editor.

**Injection mechanism, if you do go through react-markdown for a block:** override `components={{ ins: AddMark, del: DelMark, mark: HighlightMark }}`. If you ever need the marks *inside* markdown-parsed content, inject them at the **rehype/HAST level** via a small rehype plugin (build HAST `element('ins'|'del', …)` nodes wrapping the untouched math element) so `rehype-katex` still runs on intact math — **do NOT** reach for `rehype-raw` + markdown-string markers (not installed, and fragile around block/math boundaries). But the recommended path renders inline runs directly in React and sidesteps this entirely.

**Per-change UI:** floating accept ✓ / reject ✕ anchored to each change region (block banner for block ops; inline popover for inline ops), plus global **Accept all / Reject all** for the turn (Docs + Tiptap pattern).

## 4. Accept/reject data model

Model the turn as an ordered, **non-overlapping** `ChangeOp[]`, each addressing the struct precisely (mirrors OOXML `w:ins`/`w:del` and TipTap `Change{rangeA,rangeB}`):

```ts
type ChangeOp =
  | { kind:'block.insert';  at:number; block:DocBlock; id:string }
  | { kind:'block.delete';  at:number; oldBlock:DocBlock; id:string }
  | { kind:'block.move';    from:number; to:number; id:string }
  | { kind:'block.replace'; at:number; oldBlock:DocBlock; newBlock:DocBlock; inline:ChangeOp[]; id:string } // paragraph/heading/math/figure
  | { kind:'inline.ins';    blockIndex:number; runPath:number[]; offset:number; text:string; id:string }
  | { kind:'inline.del';    blockIndex:number; runPath:number[]; offset:number; text:string; id:string }
  | { kind:'frontmatter';   field:'title'|'abstract'|'keywords'; oldVal; newVal; id:string }
```

- **v1 — whole-turn.** `Accept all` → NEW struct becomes canonical; `Reject all` → keep OLD. Trivially correct, zero mapping risk. **Already wired:** `chat.apply()` / `chat.reject()` on the whole round (`PrismWorkspaceV2.tsx:251-256`). Matches Notion AI exactly (verification v2 — held), so it's the mainstream baseline, not a compromise.
- **v2 — per-change.** Each op gets `accepted: boolean`. Compute the accepted-result struct by **replaying OLD through the accepted ops only**: start from OLD; apply each accepted op at its struct address (accepted insert → keep new; rejected insert → drop; accepted delete → remove old; rejected delete → keep old; replace → new-or-old fragment); apply ops in **reverse document order** (or via a position map) so earlier edits don't shift later addresses. Because ops carry explicit addresses — not text-search context — replay is deterministic. Keep ops **non-overlapping** (merge nearby ones, à la TipTap `changeMergeDistance`) so decisions are independent. Group inline edits **per replaced block** first (TipTap `smart` granularity); expose per-word only if users demand it.
- **Write-back to the round-apply flow.** After resolution, the canonical struct = the selected merge — **no markdown re-parsing needed**. Persist via existing `useSaveStruct` (`prism.ts:372`), OR feed the reconstructed body into the existing `applyRound` `overrides` channel (`prism.ts:485-498`, `usePrismChat.ts:253-263` already supports `relPath → final body`). For v1 whole-turn, `chat.apply()` already does the right thing.

## 5. Product UX (from the survey)

- **Inline styling** = Google Docs Suggesting mode on our typeset surface: insertions green + underlined; deletions green/red **strikethrough kept in place**; both inline in the rendered doc, never a code pane.
- **Block-level markers** = a colored left gutter/banner (green added / red removed / "moved ↑↓") — the rendered-doc analog of Word's margin change-bar.
- **Per-change controls** = ✓/✕ anchored to each change (inline popover for runs, banner button for blocks) + a global Accept/Reject-all in the existing warning header (`PrismWorkspaceV2.tsx:249`). Chat-primary tools default to whole-turn (Canvas/Cursor Cmd+Enter), per-change as the escape hatch.
- **Two view modes** on the right pane (steal from Word): **Reviewing** (full inline ins/del marks) vs **Clean/Final** (typeset reading, no marks) — so KaTeX/figures stay beautiful while reading.
- **Placement** = this `StructDiffRenderer` replaces the `LatexDiffEditor` branch inside the existing right-area conditional (`PrismWorkspaceV2.tsx:245-262`); the header bar ("AI 已修改文档 — 查看变化后应用" + 放弃/应用) stays, just swapping the pane below.

## 6. Libraries

| Need | Pick | Why / limit |
|---|---|---|
| Word-level text diff inside a block | **jsdiff `diffWordsWithSpace`** (+ `intlSegmenter` for CJK) | `{value,added,removed}` → direct `<ins>/<del>`; round-trippable tokens; CJK-aware. **Not currently installed — add `diff`.** |
| Block array alignment / move detection | **jsdiff `diffArrays(a,b,{comparator})`** | one lib for both phases; comparator = id-else-type+hash; ~30 lines of move/similarity logic on top |
| Inject marks into rendered view | **`StructDiffRenderer` + react-markdown `components` override** (`ins`/`del`/`mark`) | intended extension point; renders inline runs in React, invokes KaTeX only on whole-math runs; **no `rehype-raw`** |
| Structural/attribute delta (optional) | ~~jsondiffpatch~~ | only if you want tree-shape delta; **requires `objectHash`** (our ids aren't stable → degrades to positional). jsdiff `diffArrays` gives more control over the modified-vs-add/remove threshold. Skip. |
| Rendered-HTML redline | ~~htmldiff.js~~ | **rejected**: KaTeX-span corruption (documented), lossy post-render HTML, accept/reject maps to HTML not struct |
| Code-diff pane | ~~react-diff-view / CodeMirror `unifiedMergeView`~~ | this **is** the pane we're deprecating (`LatexDiffEditor`) |
| Full editor track-changes | ~~ProseMirror suggestion-mode / changeset / Tiptap Pro~~ | best UX, but requires **replacing the react-markdown surface with a PM editor**, re-implementing KaTeX as atom nodes, + (Tiptap) a Pro license. Borrow the *pattern* (snapshot-old → compare-new → decorate with change-ids → accept=keep-new/reject=keep-old), not the dependency. Endgame only if Prism becomes a live editor. |

**Why not ProseMirror just for this:** we already hold OLD and NEW structs — `prosemirror-changeset` + `recreate-transform` exist precisely to *reconstruct* the steps we already don't need to reconstruct. Adopting it means migrating the whole reading surface off react-markdown. Its accept/reject semantics (accept = integrate + drop metadata; reject = revert) are the reference we replicate cheaply on the struct.

## 7. Implementation plan

**Phase 0 — expose NEW struct on pending (backend, small).**
- In `struct_service.go:248` `pendingStructRound`, additionally run the same `parseEditorMarkdown` + merge that `applyStructRound:216-233` does (without persisting) and return the parsed **new `DocStruct`** alongside `old_body`/`new_body`. Add `old_struct`/`new_struct` to `PendingFile` (`ws_round.go:115`). This lives in the struct-track branch (`ws_round.go:107`) and doesn't disturb the legacy file-diff path. Keeps the parser single-sourced in Go (don't port `parseEditorMarkdown` to TS).
- Extend TS `PrismPendingFile` (`prism.ts:460`) with `old_struct?: DocStruct; new_struct?: DocStruct`.
- (Alternative if backend change is undesirable v1: old-struct is already on the client; only new-struct is missing — but a JS parser would duplicate `md_bridge.go`. Prefer the backend option.)

**Phase 1 (v1 ships) — struct diff + rendered pane, whole-turn accept.**
1. `npm i diff` (jsdiff). Verify with `tsc -b` + `vite build` (docker build is stricter — per project rule).
2. New `src/features/prism/lib/struct-diff.ts`: `diffStructs(old, new): ChangeOp[]` — block `diffArrays` + similarity/move pass + intra-block `diffWordsWithSpace`; math/figure/opaque atomic.
3. New `src/features/prism/components/StructDiffRenderer.tsx`: walks `ChangeOp[]`, reuses `StructRenderer` block renderers, adds `<ins>/<del>` spans + block gutters + math/figure compare-chips. Add `.diff-ins`/`.diff-del` styles via Tailwind tokens (per `frontend-user/CLAUDE.md` style rules).
4. Wire into `PrismWorkspaceV2.tsx:262`: replace `<LatexDiffEditor …/>` with `<StructDiffRenderer old={pending.old_struct} new={pending.new_struct} />`. Keep the header's 放弃/应用 → `chat.reject()`/`chat.apply()` (whole-turn).
5. Add the **Reviewing / Clean** toggle in the pane header.
6. Deprecate `LatexDiffEditor` for the struct track (leave for legacy file-diff only).

**Phase 2 (v2) — per-change accept/reject.**
7. Render per-op ✓/✕ controls; add `accepted` state per `ChangeOp`.
8. `applyChangeOps(old, ops): DocStruct` replay-from-OLD (reverse doc order).
9. On confirm, persist via `useSaveStruct` or the `overrides` channel; whole-turn buttons become "Accept all / Reject all."
10. Refine granularity (`changeMergeDistance`-style merge, `groupInlineChanges`), CJK word segmentation, move badges.

## 8. Risks / open questions

- **Block re-id instability** (`md_bridge.go` reassigns): alignment must lean on position + content similarity; a bad similarity threshold either over-reports full-block replacements or under-reports moves. **Validate the 40% Dice threshold on real Prism edits.**
- **CJK word diffing**: default jsdiff word tokens are space-based; must pass `Intl.Segmenter('zh')` or Chinese prose shreds into char-diff confetti.
- **Inline run ↔ word-token mapping**: splitting a `bold`/`cite` run at a diff boundary while preserving marks is the fiddliest code; needs unit tests.
- **Math delimiter changes**: a paragraph that gains/loses an inline `$…$` run must route through the atomic-math path, not word-diff — guard at the run boundary.
- **Open**: do we want per-figure/asset diffing (asset id changed but caption same)? Defer to v2.
- **Open**: three view modes (clean / marked / as-if-accepted, à la Docs) or two? Two suffices for v1.

**Smallest prototype to validate the look:** a standalone story that feeds one hand-written OLD struct and one NEW struct (one modified paragraph with a bolded inserted phrase + one changed inline `$O(n)$→$O(n\log n)$` + one inserted heading) through `diffStructs` + a stub `StructDiffRenderer`, rendered with the real `MarkdownRenderer`/`rehype-katex`. Confirms (a) unchanged math stays typeset, (b) the compare-chip reads well, (c) green/red inline marks don't break KaTeX — before touching the backend or `PrismWorkspaceV2`.

## 9. Verification notes

| # | Claim | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1 | Diff at STRUCT level (align blocks → word-diff runs), render inline in React — not markdown-text (code-diff smell) nor htmldiff (KaTeX-fragile) | **HELD (supported)** | Core thesis + both rejections confirmed by markdown-diff-viewer, Liveblocks/TipTap AI copilots. Refinements folded in: it's a **two-phase** algorithm (LCS block align w/ ~40% Dice similarity → word-diff inside "modified" blocks); inject marks at **HAST/React level, not markdown text**; **math/figure/opaque are ATOMIC** (replace-whole, never diff inside — the top correctness rule on KaTeX). |
| v2 | Word/Docs render inline per-change accept/reject; whole-turn is acceptable v1 | **HELD w/ correction (partly_supported)** | Word/Docs per-change inline is confirmed as the *human-editor* gold standard. But for **AI edits specifically**, the shipping norm (Notion AI, ChatGPT Canvas whole-rewrites) is **whole-turn accept/discard/retry** — so whole-turn v1 isn't a compromise, it's the mainstream AI baseline; per-change is the natural v2 upgrade on the same data structure. |

<!-- Part VI appended by a 6-agent Unicode/CJK research workflow (agents test-compiled). -->

# Part VI — Robust Unicode/CJK text in struct→LaTeX→PDF (fixing lost Chinese, systematically)

## 1. Root cause (crisp)

Chinese is lost because **the projector never emits any CJK support package or CJK font**, for any template. The three layers break down as:

- **Engine — OK-ish.** `service.go:300` auto-switches to `xelatex` when `needsXeLaTeX(files)` returns true, and `containsCJK` (service.go:182-190) fires on Han/Kana/Hangul. So a Chinese doc *does* reach xelatex. But this is necessary, not sufficient.
- **Package — MISSING (this is the bug).** `preamble()` (projector.go:192-203) emits only `\documentclass[opts]{class}` + each template's fixed `manifest.json` package list (article: `amsmath,amssymb,graphicx,hyperref`; ieee-conf: `+cite`; etc.). **No `xeCJK`, no `ctex`, no `fontspec`, no `\setCJKmainfont` — ever.**
- **Font — present but never selected.** `texlive-lang-chinese` ships Fandol OTFs in the sandbox, but xelatex's default main font is Latin Modern, which has **no CJK glyphs**. XeLaTeX with no CJK package silently drops Han characters (missing-character warnings, no hard error) → **blank/dropped Chinese**.

**Why this is a general Unicode problem, not just Chinese:** The verification confirmed that under the current pipeline, `containsCJK` only triggers xelatex for Han/Kana/Hangul. Accented Latin (é/ñ/ü), Greek (α/β), Cyrillic, currency (€/£/¥), and emoji do **not** trigger the switch, so they stay on **pdflatex**, where raw UTF-8 for anything beyond basic Latin errors or drops. Even the CJK codepoints that *do* reach xelatex fail for lack of a font package. So the defect is architectural: **detection-driven engine switching with no Unicode/CJK preamble**. The fix must be a preamble/engine standardization, not a Chinese-specific patch.

The legacy hand-authored path (`\usepackage{ctex}` typed into a `RawLatex` block) renders Chinese fine — precisely because `loadsCJKPackage` (service.go:193) sees "ctex", forces xelatex, and ctex pulls Fandol. That confirms the sandbox fonts are adequate and the gap is entirely in `preamble()`/manifests.

## 2. Recommendation (decisive)

- **Standardize the struct track on xelatex, unconditionally.** Delete the detection dependency for the struct path — force `EngineXeLaTeX` for every struct-projected compile. The `needsXeLaTeX` heuristic is leaky (misses accented Latin/Greek/€/emoji) and is the root cause of pdflatex-path failures.
- **Always inject one class-agnostic Unicode+CJK preamble block** (not conditional). `fontspec`+`xeCJK` are visually inert on ASCII-only docs (no CJK codepoint → CJK font never invoked), so "always on" does not change the journal look. Always-on kills the leaky-detection failure mode with one code path.
- **Use `xeCJK` for ALL four templates — never the `ctex*` classes, never `ctex` as a package on journal classes.** `xeCJK` is a pure font-shaping overlay that doesn't touch sectioning/captions, so it composes with `article`, `IEEEtran`, `elsarticle`, `llncs` alike. `ctexart` *replaces* the class (can't wrap journal classes); `\usepackage{ctex}` redefines headings and collides with journal classes. Verified: xeCJK compiles clean on all four (tests B/E/F/G).
- **Set the CJK font by FILENAME, not family name.** The sandbox has **no fontconfig** (`fc-list`/`fc-cache` absent), so XeTeX resolves fonts only by filename via kpathsea. `\setCJKmainfont{FandolSong}` FAILS ("font FandolSong cannot be found" — verified test C). Use `\setCJKmainfont[BoldFont=FandolSong-Bold.otf]{FandolSong-Regular.otf}` (verified test D).
- **Accented Latin / Greek / currency need nothing beyond xelatex.** Latin Modern (the xelatex default) renders café/naïve/Zürich/€/£/¥ with 0 missing chars (verified test J2). Loading `fontspec` alone (which xeCJK pulls anyway) is enough; optionally set `\setmainfont{Latin Modern Roman}` explicitly for reproducibility.
- **Keep `escapeLaTeX`'s special set unchanged** — `\ & % $ # _ { } ~ ^` are catcode-active under xelatex too (verified test M). Add URL handling: route URLs through `\url{}` + `\usepackage{xurl}` (both present in sandbox) to stop long-URL overfull boxes.
- **No Dockerfile font change is required for baseline Chinese + accented Latin.** Fandol + Latin Modern cover them offline. Add `fonts-noto-cjk` (and an emoji font) only if you need JP/KR, rare CJK-Ext-B, or emoji glyphs — those are the only offline-unfixable gaps today.

## 3. Per-template preamble (exact lines the projector should emit)

The shared Unicode+CJK block, injected **after `\documentclass{...}` and after the class's own packages**, identical for all four templates (verified compiling on each):

```latex
% --- Unicode + CJK block (struct track, xelatex) ---
\usepackage{fontspec}
\usepackage{xeCJK}
\setCJKmainfont[BoldFont=FandolSong-Bold.otf,ItalicFont=FandolKai-Regular.otf]{FandolSong-Regular.otf}
\setCJKsansfont{FandolHei-Regular.otf}
\setCJKmonofont{FandolFang-Regular.otf}
\xeCJKsetup{AutoFakeBold=true,AutoFakeSlant=true}
\usepackage{xurl}
\sloppy
% ----------------------------------------------------
```

Notes: `AutoFakeBold/AutoFakeSlant` matter because Fandol Hei/Kai/Fang have **no Bold** — without them, bold/emphasized CJK silently falls back to regular. `\sloppy` is a global overfull safety net. `xurl` needs `hyperref` for `\url` breaking (present in article; add to the journal templates if you route URLs — see below).

**(a) article** — class already loads `hyperref`:
```latex
\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage{amsmath}\usepackage{amssymb}\usepackage{graphicx}\usepackage{hyperref}
% <shared Unicode+CJK block>
```

**(b) ieee-conf (IEEEtran)** — verified test E (`IEEEtran[conference]` + xeCJK, success). xeCJK does not touch IEEEtran's `\maketitle`/sectioning:
```latex
\documentclass[conference]{IEEEtran}
\usepackage{cite}
\usepackage{hyperref}   % add so \url/xurl work (IEEEtran doesn't load it)
% <shared Unicode+CJK block>
```

**(c) elsarticle** — verified test F:
```latex
\documentclass[preprint,12pt]{elsarticle}
\usepackage{amsmath}\usepackage{amssymb}\usepackage{graphicx}\usepackage{lineno}
\usepackage{hyperref}   % add for \url/xurl
% <shared Unicode+CJK block>
```

**(d) llncs** — verified test G; load fontspec/xeCJK **after** `\documentclass{llncs}` (llncs is load-order sensitive):
```latex
\documentclass{llncs}
\usepackage{amsmath}\usepackage{amssymb}\usepackage{graphicx}
\usepackage{hyperref}   % add for \url/xurl
% <shared Unicode+CJK block>
```

If you don't want to route URLs on the journal templates, drop the added `hyperref` and `xurl` from those three (keep `\sloppy`). But adding `hyperref` is harmless and enables clickable links + CJK bookmarks (verified test P).

## 4. Engine + when

**Struct track → always xelatex.** In `runCompile` (service.go:300-302), the struct-projected path should force `engine = EngineXeLaTeX` regardless of content, rather than depending on `needsXeLaTeX`. Rationale:

- lualatex is non-viable in this sandbox: verified test Q — `luatexja.sty` is **missing** and `luaotfload` can't find `FandolSong-Regular.otf` offline (no `luaotfload-tool`). So xelatex is the only Unicode-native engine that works here.
- The `containsCJK`/`loadsCJKPackage` detection stays useful only for the **legacy/opaque raw-`.tex`** path (user-authored files, where you can't guarantee a struct preamble). Keep `needsXeLaTeX` for that path; hard-force xelatex for struct.
- Concretely: thread an `isStruct` signal (or always-xelatex flag) from `ProjectStruct`/`StartCompile` into `runCompile` so struct compiles never take the pdflatex branch. Leave the pdflatex fallback alive only for legacy raw docs that have no CJK/Unicode.

## 5. Fonts + sandbox

- **CJK font: Fandol, by filename.** `\setCJKmainfont[BoldFont=FandolSong-Bold.otf,ItalicFont=FandolKai-Regular.otf]{FandolSong-Regular.otf}`. Files confirmed present in-container at `/usr/share/texlive/texmf-dist/fonts/opentype/public/fandol/`: `FandolSong-Regular.otf`, `FandolSong-Bold.otf`, `FandolHei-Regular/Bold.otf`, `FandolKai-Regular.otf`, `FandolFang-Regular.otf`. Only Song has Bold → hence `AutoFakeBold`.
- **General Unicode main font: Latin Modern** (xelatex default) is sufficient — verified 0 missing chars for accented Latin/currency (test J2). Optionally `\setmainfont{Latin Modern Roman}` or `TeX Gyre Termes` (both in-TEXMF, kpathsea-safe) for wider Greek/symbol coverage; not required for the baseline fix.
- **No Dockerfile change needed for baseline.** Do NOT add `fonts-noto-cjk` for baseline Chinese — Fandol works offline out of the box (verified test B: "Fandol is being set as the default font for CJK text"). Add packages only for the gaps in §7 (JP/KR, rare CJK-Ext-B → `fonts-noto-cjk` + `\setCJKmainfont{Noto Serif CJK SC}`; emoji → a color/mono emoji font — but xelatex can't embed color emoji regardless).
- **Offline / read-only gotchas:**
  - **Filename lookup bypasses fontconfig** → immune to the missing-`fc-cache`/read-only-rootfs problem. This is why the filename form is mandatory here, not just preferred.
  - If you ever switch to family-name lookup (Noto/AR PL), you MUST run `fc-cache -f` at **image-build time** (writable) so the cache is baked into the read-only layer; runtime `network_mode: none` + read-only rootfs can't rebuild it.
  - The existing writable `TEXMFVAR`/`TEXMFCACHE` tmpfs mounts cover xelatex's needs (xelatex does not use luaotfload's DB).
  - Expect and **ignore** the cosmetic log line `Font 'FandolSong-Regular' does not contain requested Script 'CJK'` — Fandol lacks OT script metadata but typesets correctly.

## 6. Escaping

**Keep the current 10-char set — it's correct and still required under xelatex** (verified test M: escaped forms compile, and `&/%/#/$/_/{/}/~/^` remain catcode-active). Verify the replacements use the **text-command, brace-terminated** forms (not accent macros): `\`→`\textbackslash{}`, `~`→`\textasciitilde{}`, `^`→`\textasciicircum{}` (projector.go:618-633 already does this — confirm `~`/`^` don't map to `\~`/`\^`, which would eat the next char).

**Now passes through raw (do NOT escape):** all letters incl. CJK, accented Latin (é/ñ/ü), Greek (α/β), Cyrillic, currency (€/£/¥) — xelatex+font handles them.

**Additions (small, correct):**
- **URLs → `\url{...}`** (with `hyperref`+`xurl`) instead of char-escaping. Raw `~`/`%`/`#`/`_` inside a URL break links if left raw, and mangle them if escaped; `\url` handles both and `xurl` breaks long ones (verified test N2: 0 overfull with `\url`+`xurl` vs 1 overfull raw).
- **Emoji → strip or placeholder** at projection time: drop U+1F000–U+1FAFF, U+2600–U+27BF, U+FE0F (variation selector), U+200D (ZWJ). No offline color-emoji rendering is possible in xelatex (verified test L: emoji fall to Latin Modern → dropped/tofu).
- **NFC-normalize input** before projecting so combining sequences (e+U+0301) become precomposed é and hit the font glyph directly.
- **Strip zero-width/format controls** (Cc/Cf: U+200B ZWSP, U+FEFF BOM, U+00AD soft hyphen, bidi controls) to avoid stray boxes.

## 7. Other robustness cases

| Failure | Cause | Mitigation | Covered by our fix? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Accented Latin é/ñ/ü | needed pdflatex+inputenc before | xelatex + Latin Modern (raw pass-through) | ✅ Covered (always-xelatex) |
| Greek α/β, Cyrillic | font coverage | xelatex + Latin Modern (or TeX Gyre Termes for wider) | ✅ Covered; ⚠️ set TeX Gyre if gaps |
| Currency € £ ¥, em-dash, curly quotes | font coverage | Latin Modern (verified 0 missing) | ✅ Covered |
| Text-mode math Unicode (±, ≤, ×, →, ∞) | font may lack glyph | `\usepackage{newunicodechar}` mapping to `\ensuremath{…}`, or wider font | ⚠️ Targeted guard (optional) |
| Emoji 😀 | xelatex can't embed color emoji; no emoji font offline | strip/replace at projection | ⚠️ Guard (strip); render needs new font+lualatex |
| Rare CJK (Ext-B, 𠀀) | Fandol lacks Ext-B | add `fonts-noto-cjk` + Noto Serif CJK SC, or CJK fallback font | ⚠️ Needs Dockerfile change if required |
| Long unbreakable URL/token | overfull hbox | `\url{}`+`xurl`; `\sloppy`/`seqsplit` for non-URL tokens | ✅ Covered (xurl+`\sloppy`) |
| Combining accents (NFD) | base+floating accent/tofu | NFC-normalize input | ⚠️ Guard (normalize) |
| Zero-width/control chars | stray boxes/spacing | strip Cc/Cf | ⚠️ Guard (strip) |
| RTL (Arabic/Hebrew) | no shaping/reordering | needs `polyglossia`+`bidi`+RTL font | ❌ Out of scope; don't crash, render LTR or flag |

## 8. Implementation plan

**`backend/internal/prism/projector.go`**
1. In `preamble()` (line 192-203), after emitting `\documentclass` + manifest packages, append the shared Unicode+CJK block from §3. Simplest: a single `emitUnicodeCJKPreamble(class)` helper that returns the block, plus `\usepackage{hyperref}` for the three journal classes that lack it. Keep it always-on.
2. Prefer sourcing the block per-template so llncs gets correct load order (block goes after the class's packages).
3. In `escapeLaTeX` (line 618-633): keep the 10 specials; add a URL pass that wraps detected URLs in `\url{...}` **before** char-escaping (so URL internals aren't mangled); add pre-passes to NFC-normalize, strip emoji, and strip zero-width/control chars. Keep these as separate sanitizer functions run on text runs (not on `RawLatex`/math blocks, which are pass-through by design).

**`backend/internal/prism/service.go`**
4. Force `engine = EngineXeLaTeX` on the struct-projected compile path in `runCompile` (line 300-302) — thread an `isStruct`/`forceXeLaTeX` flag from `StartCompile`/`ProjectStruct`. Leave `needsXeLaTeX` for the legacy raw-`.tex` path only.

**`prism_tex/Dockerfile`**
5. **No change required to ship the fix.** Only if emoji/rare-CJK/JP-KR coverage is later needed: add `fonts-noto-cjk` (and run `fc-cache -f` at build time), then switch `\setCJKmainfont` to `Noto Serif CJK SC` or add it as a CJK fallback family.

**Verification (compile a struct with mixed content → inspect PDF):**
```bash
# after rebuild, compile a struct doc containing: 中文测试 café naïve Zürich α≤β € https://example.com/very/long/path?x=1
docker exec -it scholar_prism_tex sh -lc 'kpsewhich FandolSong-Regular.otf'   # returns TEXMF path (offline-safe)
docker exec -it scholar_prism_tex sh -lc 'latexmk -xelatex -interaction=nonstopmode main.tex'
# check log for "Missing character" — should be NONE for CJK/accented; grep the PDF text layer for 中文/café
```
Verify the PDF shows the Chinese glyphs, accented Latin, and a wrapped (non-overflowing) URL. Confirm 0 "Missing character" warnings for CJK and accented Latin.

**Ships first:** (1) always-xelatex for struct + (2) the injected `fontspec`+`xeCJK`+Fandol-by-filename block. That alone fixes lost Chinese and accented Latin — the highest-value, zero-Dockerfile-change slice. URL/emoji/normalize sanitizers ship second; Noto/emoji font third (only if needed).

## 9. Risks / open questions

- **Journal-class visual drift from always-on fontspec.** xeCJK/fontspec on ASCII-only journal docs is inert for CJK, but `fontspec` can subtly change the Latin main font. Verified English-only IEEEtran/elsarticle compile clean (tests S/T), but confirm the *rendered look* matches each class's default. Mitigation: set `\setmainfont` to each class's expected face (Latin Modern for article; the journal classes are Times-like → `TeX Gyre Termes` if drift appears), or omit `\setmainfont` entirely and let the class default stand.
- **Only Song has Bold in Fandol.** `AutoFakeBold` covers it, but faux-bold CJK looks slightly worse than a real bold face — acceptable, note it.
- **Emoji and rare CJK-Ext-B remain unfixable offline** without adding fonts (and emoji needs lualatex/HarfBuzz for color). Decide: strip (recommended) vs. add fonts.
- **RTL unsupported** — ensure the sanitizer at least doesn't crash on Arabic/Hebrew.
- **Smallest verification:** compile one struct doc per template (article/IEEEtran/elsarticle/llncs) each containing `中文 café α≤β € <long URL>`; assert 0 CJK/accented "Missing character" warnings and a non-overflowing URL in all four PDFs.
